title: Prompt Bootleg Sandbox
content:
Quick scratchpad for small experiments — night-shift bootleg of prompt templates, a handful of few-shot sets, and ad-hoc failure probes. Not polished. Use liberally, break things, note reproducibility quirks.

Context and goal:
- Trying to build tiny, resilient exemplar packs that work across: hosted-api (gpt-like), a quantized v2 model, and a trimmed low-token SLO case.
- Want compact few-shot sets (<= 3 examples) that encourage structured output (yaml/json) while avoiding hallucination on entity fields.
- Track failure modes and quick mitigation heuristics.

Running hypothesis:
- Short, explicit delimiters + labeled examples reduce hallucination on key fields more than added instruction text when token budget is tight.
- Rotating distractor examples across few-shot sets reduces brittle overfitting to phrasing.

Template bank (rough) — experiment names and first-pass templates:
1) compact-kv-template-v1
   """
   You are a precise extractor. Given the text, return a JSON object with fields: name, date, amount. If any field is missing, use null. Do not add commentary.

   ---START EXAMPLE---
   Text: "Invoice from Servo Labs dated 2024-11-03 for $2,450 to Acme Corp."
   Output: {"name": "Servo Labs", "date": "2024-11-03", "amount": 2450}
   ---END EXAMPLE---

   Input: {user_text}
   Output:
   """
   Notes: keep tokens minimal, prefer numeric amounts (no $).

2) labeled-blocks-yaml-v2
   - Ask for YAML explicit mapping, include "confidence": low/med/high depending on missing fields. Two-shot where examples include edgecases (ranges, words for numbers).

3) instruction-plus-guardrails-v0.3
   - Longer instruction but contains a final "If you are unsure, return ONLY: {\"uncertain\": true}" guard. Useful for safety gating but increases tokens.

Few-shot sets to try (labelled by intent) — keep as canonical examples to rotate:
- FS-INV-SHORT (2 examples): clean invoices only, different phrasings ("dated", "on")
- FS-INV-WEIRD (3 examples): includes textual amounts ("two thousand"), ambiguous dates ("last Monday")
- FS-NEG-SHIELD (1 example + negative): shows a text that is NOT an invoice to teach negative classification

Observed failure modes (notes from quick runs):
- Mode A: "invented-sender" — model returns a plausible company name when none present. Happens when few-shot examples include many senders.
  Mitigation attempts: add explicit "use null if sender not present" in header; provide negative example where sender missing. Reduction observed but not eliminated under quantized model.

- Mode B: "date-normalization-lag" — model outputs human text like "Nov 3rd" instead of ISO. Fix with explicit example outputs in ISO and a final requirement line: "Dates must be YYYY-MM-DD or null".

- Mode C: "currency-verbosity" — model returns "$2,450 USD (two thousand...)" when instructions asked numeric. Quick fix: enforce "amount must be an integer number of cents" — but this increases user friction.

Micro-experiments and transcripts (fast test logs):
- 2025-01-14 02:10 (hosted-api, temp key)
  Prompt: compact-kv-template-v1 + FS-INV-SHORT
  Input text: "Payment received from ByteIO for 3000 on 2024-12-12"
  Output: {name: "ByteIO", date: "2024-12-12", amount: 3000}  // good

- 2025-01-15 23:42 (dedicated-sim, quantized v2)
  Prompt: same as above but with FS-INV-WEIRD
  Input text: "Invoice: Services rendered. Total: two thousand five hundred. Issued Nov 3."
  Output: {name: "Services rendered", date: "Nov 3", amount: "two thousand five hundred"}  // fails normalization + sender hallucination

Notes-to-self:
- Run with instruction-plus-guardrails on quantized runner and compare token cost difference (quick A/B). Record latency + token counts.
- Try negative sampling: include 1/3 negative examples in the few-shot pack to teach abstain.
- Try prefix caching of system instruction vs embedding it each request (cost tradeoffs).

Edge experiments to schedule:
- Adversarial short text: "Paid to: [illegible]" — check robustness.
- Cascaded verification trick: first pass extract minimal fields, second pass reformat/validate. Measure extra latency vs error reduction.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How stable are these heuristics when we route to fallback models? e.g., will the guardrail string survive when we switch to a lower-quality variant via smart routing? Need to reproduce with routing table that triggers fallback.
- Is including an explicit negative example better than an extra instruction line? tradeoff: examples cost tokens but may be more effective.

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] schedule 3 dedicated runs comparing: compact-kv-template-v1 vs instruction-plus-guardrails-v0.3 vs labeled-blocks-yaml-v2
- [ ] instrument token counts and latency (per-run) and add CSV to drive (link below)
- [ ] open a small GH PR adding the top-2 templates to /prompt-registry (draft) for others to reuse
- [ ] drop 1-2 canonical negative examples into FS-INV-WEIRD set and retest

References and quick links:
- See draft PR: github:redwood-inference/prompt-registry/pull/912 (branch: maya/prompt-bootleg)
- Linear ticket for instrumentation: linear:INF-1127
- Slack thread: #prompt-lab-thread-3 (pinned messages include sample transcripts)

Random scratch thoughts:
- Maybe create a tiny "token-frugal" template that compresses example outputs by replacing labels with single-letter keys and then translate back in a postprocessing step — might help with SLOs but brittle for maintainability.
- Keep a micro-benchmark: 200 samples / template / model variant, run overnight, save CSV.

If you read this and feel like playing: copy templates to prompt-registry as draft, add a tiny test harness (python script in pr) that runs across hosted + dedicated-sim and dumps results in /tmp for now.

-- maya
